title: Career roadmap · Deep-tech Founder
summary: A research-to-venture pathway focused on turning scientific or engineering research into defensible technology, a validated product, a funded company and scalable commercial impact.

facts.Timeline assumption: 2026 is treated as Ph.D. Year 1. The roadmap assumes that the Ph.D. provides access to a research problem or technology that can potentially become a product or venture. The founder path should remain research-led while progressively adding customer discovery, IP, product development, fundraising and company-building experience.

rows.text: Deep-tech opportunity discovery and problem selection
Produce a 10-problem landscape and select 3 research-backed opportunities
Complete 20+ documented stakeholder interviews and identify one priority problem
Demonstrate a working prototype and document its TRL assumptions
Complete prior-art research and an invention-disclosure package
Business model, market sizing and pricing
Build a business model and interview-backed market-sizing model
Run at least one structured pilot with documented success criteria
Prepare an investor data room, pitch deck and 3-year financial model
Prepare incorporation, founder-equity, IP-ownership and governance checklist
Thesis + prototype + IP + customer evidence + funding strategy + company plan

blocks.text: After product-market fit, shift from technical founder to company builder. Develop executive capability in hiring, capital allocation, regulatory strategy, international markets, partnerships and multi-product R&D while retaining enough technical depth to guide the technology roadmap.

blocks.label: Job-posting note
blocks.text: For founder-track positions, current employer postings are only one signal. Incubators and investors will also examine the technology, customer evidence, IP position, founding team and commercial traction.

A second postgraduate degree is generally not the default after this Ph.D. For a founder, incubator participation, translational research, industry pilots and venture financing are usually more directly relevant.

Career progression

Ph.D. Researcher → Venture Builder / Technology Commercialisation Fellow → Founder/Co-founder
2030–2035: Founder → Seed-stage CEO/CTO → Product-market-fit leader
2035–2040: Growth-stage Founder/CEO → R&D and commercialisation leader → Multi-product company builder
2040–2046: Founder/CEO → Deep-Tech Group Executive → Serial Founder / Board-level Technology Entrepreneur

If further research is pursued after this Ph.D., relevant areas include:

A successful deep-tech founder eventually needs to operate across three systems: technology, capital and markets. The priority becomes building a durable R&D organisation, protecting the company's technical advantage, allocating capital between research and commercial products, recruiting scientific and commercial leaders, expanding internationally and deciding when to create additional ventures. Remaining technically credible while becoming an effective CEO is the central long-term challenge.
